title: The Hand-Off Test
document_title: Agent Field Notes No. 004 — The Hand-Off Test

source.name: GitHub Changelog
source.title: GitHub Copilot app, Microsoft Ignite releases

verified_facts.claim: The GitHub Copilot app now supports Azure DevOps repositories.
verified_facts.quote: The GitHub Copilot app now supports your Azure DevOps repositories, your GitHub Enterprise Server instance

verified_facts.claim: An agent can create a branch, make code changes and open a pull request, then see it through to completion without leaving the app.
verified_facts.quote: Clone an Azure DevOps repository, ask an agent to create a branch, make code changes, and open a pull request, then see it through to completion without leaving the GitHub Copilot app.

verified_facts.claim: Track the PR in the sidebar and click Fix on a review comment.
verified_facts.quote: Track its status in the sidebar, click Fix on a review comment to have an agent address it

verified_facts.claim: Agent merge fixes CI failures and completes the PR once Azure DevOps checks and policies pass.
verified_facts.quote: turn on agent merge to let an agent fix CI failures and complete the pull request once your Azure DevOps checks and policies pass

verified_facts.claim: Azure DevOps integration is in public preview.
verified_facts.quote: Azure DevOps integration is now in public preview.

verified_facts.claim: Turn it on under Settings > Experimental.
verified_facts.quote: To get started, open Settings > Experimental and turn on Azure DevOps integration

verified_facts.claim: Sign in under Accounts > Add account with the Microsoft account used for Azure DevOps.
verified_facts.quote: then go to Accounts > Add account and sign in with the Microsoft account you use for Azure DevOps.

verified_facts.claim: Cloud sessions aren't available for Azure DevOps repos.
verified_facts.quote: Cloud sessions aren’t available for Azure DevOps repositories.

verified_facts.claim: On Azure DevOps, Claude can watch your branch for up to seven days.
verified_facts.quote: On a host other than GitHub, such as GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps, Claude can watch your branch for up to seven days.

verified_facts.claim: In a terminal session, Claude Code can read the PR's checks and comments.
verified_facts.quote: In a terminal session, Claude Code can read details such as your open merge request or pull request, its checks, and its comments.

verified_facts.claim: /ship and /steward run from the Claude Code CLI in a terminal.
verified_facts.quote: Run either command from the Claude Code CLI in a terminal, in your local clone of the repository.

verified_facts.claim: On Azure DevOps, you push your branch yourself.
verified_facts.quote: Commit your change first, then push your branch with an upstream from your shell

verified_facts.claim: On Azure DevOps, you open the pull request yourself.
verified_facts.quote: On gitlab.com, bitbucket.org, or dev.azure.com, open your merge request or pull request next.

verified_facts.claim: The watch has no command to reply to comments, re-run a check or read CI logs there.
verified_facts.quote: The watch gives Claude no command to reply to comments, re-run a check, or read CI logs there.
once the pull request is ready, merge it yourself
